newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX index ends at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX index ends at record closing high.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index continued its record-breaking rally on Monday and ended at an all time closing high, with market players revising their outlooks for the index upwards to 3,600/3,700 points for 1997.

The IBIS DAX ended up 74.61 points, or 2.14 percent, at 3,565.69 points, just shy of an all-time high of 3,566.60 points, with trading sentiment boosted by an upbeat start on the Dow Jones industrial index on Wall Street.
The dollar continued to provide support, having earlier contributed to a record closing high on the DAX index of 3,528.78 points.
"What we have here is problem-free growth and the index keeps rising," said one Frankfurt trader.
Another trader said that after the massive jump in the first quarter, the markets were a bit nervous and the month of April signalled a bit of a consolidation phase.
"But now we may be getting an external impulse so people might just take up where they left off in April. If we don't get any massive dirt from the U.S. this may be sustainable," the trader said.
He also said that he thought there may be a need for short term consolidation back toward 3,480 if any significant gains were to be achieved.

Among financial stocks, Dresdner Bank ended up 2.43 marks or 4.34 percent at 58.45 marks. Dealers said it was in a strong technical position and that sentiment was lifted by long-running speculation about changes in the shape of the banking sector.

Other big gainers in the afternoon were airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG, up 4.03 percent at 25.80 marks, and diversified utility RWE AG, up 2.11 marks at 73.63 marks, which illustrates how the gains were really across the board in afternoon IBIS trade.
Software group SAP AG fell more than four percent earlier to 314 marks after Frankfurt prosecutors said they were probing a potentially serious insider trading case involving the company.
Dealers downplayed the move, noting that SAP is notoriously volatile. By the end of the day the share was up 2.05 marks at 330 marks.
"The dollar is stable, the debt market is strong and the U.S. helped us last Friday," a trader said.
